From: Tom Reese <tom.reese@novacorp.com>

Cc: ops@papertrail.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Unexpected 503s from inference endpoint (impacting production)

Avery,

We started seeing a spike in 503s on our inference endpoint around 12:35pm PT. The errors are affecting our checkout flow for a subset (~8%) of customers. Our SREs captured a few stack traces and a short window of request logs — attaching the excerpt. Can you confirm if Redwood has an ongoing issue or if this looks like traffic pattern at our end?

We’re on standby; would appreciate a rapid triage.

- Tom
Novacorp, Sr. Platform Engineer

Attachments: 2026-07-20_novacorp-error-log.txt (text)
From: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
To: Tom Reese <tom.reese@novacorp.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RE: Unexpected 503s from inference endpoint (impacting production)

Tom — thanks for the flag and the logs. I’ve opened an incident and engaged ops; see quick summary and immediate next steps below. I’ll keep you updated every 30 minutes until mitigated.

Immediate summary (as of 13:28 PT):
- Observed: Elevated 503 errors for production model endpoint rwd-std-1, starting ~12:35 PT.
- Impact: ~6–9% of requests returning 503s; higher latency on retries.
- Likely vectors under investigation: kernel OOM on GPU hosts, and a surge of very long-sequence requests triggering autoscale contention.

What we are doing now:
1) Ops lead (Ben) is running a targeted host sweep to isolate any GPU host-level failures.
2) We have increased autoscaling headroom on Novacorp’s Dedicated pool and temporarily activated burst capacity.
3) We’ve enabled a short-lived rate limiter on long-sequence requests to protect the pool while preserving ~90% of normal traffic.

Ask of Novacorp: can your team provide any recent workload changes (new prompts, bulk batch jobs) started shortly before 12:35 PT? That will help correlate.

Attaching incident reference and ticket for traceability: INC-9832. I will share an executive note once we have containment.

- Avery
Avery Johnson | Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0183

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Reese <tom.reese@novacorp.com>, ops@papertrail.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 14:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RE: Unexpected 503s from inference endpoint (impacting production)

Quick ops update and containment actions taken:

Status at 14:01 PT:
- Root cause (preliminary): one GPU host in the Dedicated pool experienced a CUDA kernel OOM when serving a very long-sequence request. The host failed fast and triggered a brief cascade while autoscaler brought up replacement capacity.
- Containment: replacement hosts are active; burst capacity held while we patch the autoscale thresholds. Rate limiter on >3k token requests is active (rolling back after validation).

Customer-facing mitigations completed:
- Failover of requests away from the problematic host completed at 13:47 PT.
- Temporary restriction on long-sequence single-call generation to prevent further OOMs.
- A rolling restart of 3 adjacent hosts was executed to clear residual kernel state.

Planned follow-ups (next 24 hours):
- Patch autoscaler threshold and increase warm pool sizing for the Dedicated cluster (ETA: 6 hours).
- Collect full host diagnostics and a block-level kernel trace (ETA: 4 hours).
- Run targeted load test to reproduce long-sequence OOM locally (engineering).

We’ll maintain a 30-min cadence for updates; I’ll post the kernel traces and the remediation checklist to INC-9832 once available.

- Ben
Ben Carter | Ops Lead, Redwood Inference

From: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
To: Tom Reese <tom.reese@novacorp.com>, Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@novacorp.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:43:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood incident update: containment achieved and next steps (INC-9832)

Tom / Sarah — quick executive update and commitments following the outage yesterday. Thanks for the patience and for sending logs — that accelerated diagnosis.

What happened (plain language):
- Between ~12:35–13:50 PT on 20 Jul, a small subset of requests (~6–9%) received 503s due to a GPU host-level CUDA OOM that caused a brief cascade while the autoscaler replaced capacity.

What we did (customer-facing):
- Immediate failover of traffic away from the affected hosts and activation of burst capacity to preserve throughput.
- Temporary safeguards: rate-limited extremely long-sequence single calls (affects <0.5% of your traffic) until autoscaler thresholds are patched.
- Rolling restarts and kernel trace captures for forensics.

Customer impact and mitigation:
- Impact window: ~12:35–13:50 PT on 20 Jul.
- Observed user-facing effect: increased 503s and retry latency for ~6–9% of requests during the window. No request-level data loss detected.

Our commitments and timeline:
- Within 4 hours: post full host-level diagnostics and kernel traces to INC-9832 (Ben).
- Within 6 hours: deploy autoscaler threshold patch and increase warm pool sizing for your Dedicated pool; we will monitor for 24 hours post-deploy (Ben).
- Within 48 hours: full postmortem and recommended preventative changes, including config suggestions for long-sequence request handling and SDK retry guidance (Marissa + Engineering).
- Credits: We will evaluate the incident under our SLA and reach out with a proposed credit amount within 5 business days (Finance).

Interim guidance for Novacorp engineers:
- If you can, avoid batched long-sequence inference calls for the next 48 hours or keep them under 3,000 tokens where possible.
- If you have a non-production window we can run a load test against, we’ll coordinate to validate the warm pool sizing changes.

Escalation contacts (for exec/contract questions):
- Avery Johnson (Account lead) — avery_johnson@redwood.ai, +1 (415) 555-0183
- Vivek Kulkarni (Head of Customer Success) — vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Next update: I’ll send a follow-up when the autoscaler patch is live (ETA: ~6 hours). If anything changes faster I’ll notify immediately.

Thanks,
Avery
Avery Johnson | Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference platform
